## New Year in Brazil: Copacabana, Iguazu, the Amazon and Búzios

**This itinerary is for travelers who want to welcome the New Year beside the ocean and then explore several of Brazil's natural regions.** The group trip is scheduled for **December 30, 2026 – January 10, 2027**, lasting 12 days and 11 nights.

The journey starts in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with New Year's Eve on Copacabana Beach. Next come [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), an Amazon lodge near [Manaus](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/) and a final stay on the beaches of [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/).

The program involves several flights and frequent changes of natural scenery. It is very different from [Carnival tours](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-beach-12-days/): the central event here is **New Year's Eve on December 31**, not the February samba school parade at the Sambadrome.

## Where New Year is celebrated and what the Rio stay includes

The first four nights are spent in Rio. On December 31, an excursion to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado is scheduled, followed by celebrations on Copacabana. The next day includes city sightseeing and Sugarloaf Mountain. A separate day is left free.

New Year's Eve on Copacabana differs from a private hotel event. The public celebration takes place beside the ocean among large crowds, making it important to agree on a meeting point, stay in contact with the group and arrange transport afterward. **Dinner and admission to a separate hotel party are not automatically included**; these are additional options.

There is enough time to discover the city's main panoramas, but not for a week-long stay in Rio: on January 3, the journey already continues to Iguazu.

## Why there are two excursion days at Iguazu

Three nights are planned in [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). After arriving, travelers visit the Brazilian side of the falls and then [the Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

The Brazilian walkways offer broad panoramic views of the waterfall system. The Argentine park allows visitors to approach individual cascades and see the Devil's Throat from another angle. Visiting Argentina requires a border crossing and attention to entry rules for each traveler's nationality.

The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as possible extra excursions, but **they are not free parts of the mandatory program**. The actual availability of walking routes in both national parks must also be considered before the trip.

## Two nights in the Amazon: why flight times matter

After Iguazu, travelers fly to Manaus and stay for two nights at a lodge surrounded by Amazon forest. The program includes a boat excursion and an introduction to local traditions and a Caboclo village. Activities such as piranha fishing may be available, but this is an introduction to the region's nature, not a separate professional fishing expedition.

The key logistical condition concerns arrival and departure times. **To use the included group transfer to the lodge, you must arrive in Manaus before 16:00 and depart after 14:30.** With flights outside these windows, a private transfer costs extra. This matters especially because domestic air tickets themselves are not included in the tour.

Russian-speaking guides are provided in Rio and Iguazu, while the Amazon section has English-speaking assistance. Do not assume the same Russian-speaking specialist accompanies the group throughout every stage.

## How the 12 days are divided

| Stop | Nights |
|---|---:|
| Rio de Janeiro | 4 |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 3 |
| Amazon lodge | 2 |
| Búzios | 2 |

On day ten, the group returns from Manaus to Rio and transfers to Búzios. After the busy sightseeing program, there is free time on the coast, followed by a transfer for the international flight home. Two nights in Búzios provide a short break by the ocean rather than a full week-long beach holiday.

## What's included and how to assess the price

The package includes accommodation along the itinerary, scheduled group excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Rio and Iguazu, English-speaking assistance in Manaus and group transfers. International and domestic flights, additional events, meals and drinks outside the specified inclusions, and tips are paid for separately.

Prices for accommodation in 4-star hotels start **from USD 5,846 per person in a triple room**; the double-room option starts **from USD 6,401**. Different rates apply to 5-star hotels. Compare options with the same hotel category and room occupancy, adding flight expenses separately.

Additional programs have separate prices: the Bird Park, Macuco Safari, Meeting of the Waters and swimming with pink dolphins. None should be treated as an automatically included part of the basic excursion package.

## Frequently asked questions about New Year in Brazil

### Is New Year's Eve celebrated during Carnival?

No. New Year is celebrated on Copacabana on the night of December 31, 2026, to January 1, 2027. The samba school parade at the Sambadrome takes place at a different time of year.

### Can we see the Argentine side of Iguazu?

Yes. The program includes a separate excursion day near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), involving a border crossing.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. They are paid for separately. When choosing Manaus flights, the time restrictions for the group transfer to the lodge are especially important.

### How much time is spent relaxing in Búzios?

Two nights and one free day before the final airport transfer.

## New Year in Brazil in 10 days: Rio, Iguazu and Búzios

**Tour dates are December 30, 2026 – January 8, 2027.** The first three nights are in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the next three in [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), and the final three on the coast, primarily in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). The program combines a holiday celebration, nature excursions and a substantial break by the ocean.

Its main difference from the [seven-day Rio–Iguazu tour](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-new-year-7-days/) is the three-night beach stay at the end. Travelers who only want festive Rio and city excursions without domestic flights can choose a separate [five-day tour](/brazil/tour/rio-new-year-copacabana-christ-redeemer-sugarloaf/).

## Rio: December 30, New Year's Eve and January 1

On arrival day, a hotel transfer and free time are planned. On December 31, the program takes travelers to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. In the evening, the New Year is celebrated on Copacabana amid music, people dressed in white and festivities beside the ocean. A New Year's restaurant dinner can be booked separately; it is not included in the basic package.

January 1 includes an ascent to Sugarloaf Mountain via Urca and an introduction to Rio's historic center. Attraction schedules and traffic arrangements may change during the holidays. Rio's authorities traditionally impose special vehicle access restrictions around Copacabana; the exact hours for the celebrations welcoming 2027 must be checked against municipal announcements, not last year's arrangements.

## Iguazu: two days, two national parks

On January 2, travelers fly to Foz do Iguaçu. On January 3, they explore the [Brazilian side of the falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), which offers broad panoramas of the cascades. On January 4, there is an excursion to [the Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where trails run at different elevations and an ecological train leads toward the Devil's Throat area.

These are different views of the same waterfall system. Visiting the Argentine side involves crossing the border, and the required travel documents depend on each visitor's nationality. High water can sometimes restrict access to individual walkways, so the opening of every viewpoint on a particular date cannot be guaranteed.

The Bird Park can be booked as an extra for **$50 per person**, and Macuco Safari for **$130**. Neither is automatically included in the base price.

## Beach time: Búzios or another resort

On January 5, after a flight from Iguazu to Rio, the program includes a transfer to [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). Free days follow, with time for bays, beaches and optional boat excursions. On January 8, travelers return to Rio's airport.

Alternative beach regions include [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/), [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/), [Jericoacoara](/brazil/place/jericoacoara/), [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/) and [Porto Seguro](/brazil/place/porto-seguro/). **These are possible replacements for the beach destination, not additional stops for every traveler.** More distant resorts usually require changes to domestic flight arrangements and the budget.

## Price and included services

| Section of the journey | Nights |
|---|---:|
| Rio | 3 |
| Iguazu | 3 |
| Coast | 3 |

Prices for the **10-day / 9-night** tour start **from $3,532**. Hotels, group excursions with a Russian-speaking guide and group transfers are included. International and domestic flights, optional excursions, meals and drinks beyond the stated program, tips and laundry are paid for separately.

The standard route requires at least two domestic flights: Rio–Iguazu and Iguazu–Rio. This matters when calculating the full cost, particularly if a distant beach region is selected instead of Búzios.

Late December and January are summer months in Brazil. Non-slip shoes and protection from spray are useful on Iguazu's viewing trails; in Rio, bring sun protection and allow extra time for holiday traffic restrictions.

## Frequently asked questions about the 10-day New Year tour

### What are the scheduled dates?

December 30, 2026 – January 8, 2027.

### Is the Argentine side of Iguazu included?

Yes, it is part of the main itinerary on January 4. Border-crossing requirements depend on the traveler's nationality.

### Can we choose Angra dos Reis instead of Búzios?

Yes. An alternative beach region is possible. Flights, transfers and the price must be agreed for the chosen option.

### Are air tickets included?

No. Both international and domestic flights are paid for separately.

## 16-day New Year VIP tour of Brazil: from Rio to Bonito and the Atlantic coast

The [New Year VIP tour of Brazil with Bonito](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-vip-bonito-rio-iguazu-16-days/) lasts **16 days and 15 nights**. The program begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with New Year's celebrations on Copacabana, continues to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), then reaches [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), with its clear rivers and caves. The final extended stage is devoted to a beach holiday in [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/).

The main question when choosing this itinerary is whether you are comfortable taking several domestic flights to see very different regions of Brazil. Long transfers separate the city celebrations, waterfalls, snorkeling and beach days. The comfort of the journey depends on a well-planned sequence of days as much as on the hotels.

## What makes this particular program VIP?

This tour names specific hotels and room categories, so its premium offering can be assessed through actual accommodation rather than a VIP label alone.

| Stage | Hotel specified in the program |
|---|---|
| Rio | Copacabana Palace |
| Iguazu | Hotel das Cataratas |
| Bonito | Arte da Natureza |
| Coast | Nannai Muro Alto |

Four nights in Rio are planned at **Copacabana Palace, A Belmond Hotel**, in a One Bedroom Double Suite. At Iguazu, the selected hotel is **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas**, located inside the national park. In Bonito, accommodation is at **Arte da Natureza Hotel Bonito**, and the beach stay is at **Nannai Muro Alto** in a bungalow.

The specific room and meal arrangements are checked against the [current tour program](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-vip-bonito-rio-iguazu-16-days/) when booking. The program allows hotels to be replaced with alternatives of a comparable category, so a hotel name should not be treated as an unconditional guarantee before final confirmation.

## New Year in Rio and the sightseeing days

The first part of the trip is devoted to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). It includes excursions to Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado, an introduction to the historic center and a private boat outing to [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/). Day five is left free for relaxation and New Year's celebrations on Copacabana.

It is important to distinguish staying in the city for the holiday from purchasing additional festive services. Access to a particular party, a restaurant table or a private fireworks-viewing venue cannot be regarded as included without separate confirmation. The dates of a specific New Year departure and the celebration option must be clarified: no separate fixed departure calendar has yet been established.

## Iguazu: a hotel inside the park and the cascades

After Rio, travelers fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The program provides accommodation at Hotel das Cataratas and a walk on the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, reaching the Devil's Throat area.

If you are interested in more activities, remember that helicopter flights and separate excursions are not automatically included simply because this is a VIP journey. Compare the core itinerary and the particular optional modules, then select additions according to the available time and conditions.

## Bonito: rivers, caves and natural pools

In [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), the nature of the journey changes. The main experiences include snorkeling in the clear waters of the [Sucuri River](/brazil/place/sucuri-river/), visiting the [Blue Lake Cave](/brazil/place/blue-lake-cave-bonito/) and walking to the waterfalls of Estancia Mimosa.

Snorkeling takes place at the water's surface with a mask and snorkel. It should not be described as scuba diving: these are different activities with different requirements. A visit to the Abismo Anhumas cave is listed among related excursion possibilities, but the availability of that descent and whether it is included in the price must be confirmed separately.

Visiting Bonito also requires time for transfers from Campo Grande. Reducing the program by one day could therefore mean losing a separate nature excursion rather than simply one overnight stay.

## A beach finale in Porto de Galinhas

After Bonito, the route continues via Recife to [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/), where several days are devoted to beach relaxation. There are fewer mandatory long transfers during this stage than earlier in the trip. Accommodation is planned at Nannai Muro Alto, near the reef-lined coast of Muro Alto.

This ending suits travelers who want to spend time by the ocean after an intensive sightseeing program. The beach days form a substantial part of the tour, so comparing the entire product with a short “Rio + Iguazu” trip on price alone would be misleading.

## What to include in your budget

Confirmed inclusions are accommodation, excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Rio and Iguazu, English-speaking assistance on excursions in Bonito, transfers and entrance tickets under the program. **Domestic flights cost extra**: they connect Rio, Iguazu, Campo Grande, Recife and the return journey via Rio. Optional activities and some meals are also excluded from the base package.

Premium journeys should therefore be compared by their full cost structure. See the main fare and list of services on the [specific 16-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-vip-bonito-rio-iguazu-16-days/), and other formats among [VIP tours in Brazil](/vip/brazil/).

## Frequently asked questions about the New Year VIP tour

### Is Bonito part of the main itinerary?

Yes. Separate days in Bonito feature the Sucuri River, Blue Lake Cave and the waterfalls of Estancia Mimosa. This is an important part of the tour between Iguazu and the beach holiday.

### Are all flights included in the price?

No. Domestic flights are specifically listed among costs outside the main package. Their route and price must be taken into account when comparing offers.

### Does the program include New Year's Eve on Copacabana?

The itinerary sets aside a free day for the celebration on Copacabana. The terms of the specific New Year departure and any extra festive services are agreed before booking.

## Private 13-day Brazil tour: cities, waterfalls and islands

This journey is for travelers interested in discovering different sides of Brazil during a single vacation. The first days are devoted to the panoramas and history of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), followed by [the Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In the northeast, travelers visit [Recife](/brazil/place/recife/) and [Olinda](/brazil/place/olinda/), the beaches of [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/) and the marine nature of [Fernando de Noronha](/brazil/place/fernando-de-noronha/).

**The 13 days and 12 nights** are divided among five stops: 3 nights in Rio, 2 at Iguazu, 2 in Recife, 2 in Porto de Galinhas and 3 on Fernando de Noronha. This is a private itinerary with scheduled meetings and transfers. It requires several domestic flights, making connections between regions and airline baggage allowances especially important.

## Who will enjoy this itinerary?

For first-time visitors to Brazil who want to combine famous landmarks with beach days, the program reveals more of the country than the familiar “Rio and Iguazu” pairing. Each stage has a distinct purpose: city sightseeing, discovering the falls, the historical architecture of the northeast, relaxed swimming and observing marine nature.

If your main goal is to spend almost the entire vacation by the ocean, flights between five stops may feel too frequent. For a longer stay in one seaside location, compare [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) with fewer transfers.

## How the days and experiences are divided

| Days | Main focus |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Rio panoramas, Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado |
| 4–5 | Iguazu Falls and walks in the park |
| 6–7 | Recife and the historic center of Olinda |
| 8–9 | Pernambuco beaches and natural pools |
| 10–13 | Fernando de Noronha archipelago |

**Rio.** The two half-day city excursions offer different experiences. The cable car to Sugarloaf Mountain provides views of bays and city districts, while the train to Christ the Redeemer passes through Tijuca Forest. This sightseeing stage is followed by long-distance travel.

**Iguazu.** The main itinerary includes the Brazilian side of the falls, with panoramic trails and broad views of the cascades. [The Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) is offered separately, with an English-speaking guide. It must not be treated as already included: visiting another country, travel documents and time for the border crossing all require separate arrangements. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are also optional activities in the Iguazu area.

**Pernambuco.** In [Recife](/brazil/place/recife/) and [Olinda](/brazil/place/olinda/), the itinerary focuses on bridges, canals, old churches and colonial architecture. The pace then changes: at [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/), time at the ocean can be planned around the tides. Natural pools among the reefs are best seen at low water, while sea conditions on exposed beaches differ from sheltered reef areas.

**Fernando de Noronha.** The archipelago includes a full 4×4 sightseeing excursion visiting natural areas, bays and viewpoints. A separate free day is reserved for relaxation or optional activities such as a boat trip, trekking or scuba diving. The list of available activities is broader than the paid program, so specific extras must be arranged separately.

## Particular considerations for visiting Fernando de Noronha

[Fernando de Noronha](/brazil/place/fernando-de-noronha/) is a protected archipelago where access to some natural areas is separately regulated. The authorities charge visitors an environmental fee, **TPA**, based on the duration of their stay. Before departure, confirm the applicable amount, payment procedure and whether the fee is included in the private quotation. Also check access rules for the beaches and trails you plan to visit.

Three nights on the islands are enough for an introduction to the bays and one free day, although weather and sea conditions may affect activities on the water. Encounters with dolphins or sea turtles cannot be guaranteed. For marine excursions, confirm participation requirements and whether advance reservations are necessary.

## What's included in the tour price and what costs extra

The program includes **4-star hotels with breakfast, guided excursions and chauffeured transfers**. International flights, domestic flights, meals beyond the stated inclusions and optional excursions are paid for separately. When comparing quotations, it is therefore particularly important to add all flights to the land arrangements: Rio–Iguazu, onward travel to Recife, flights to the archipelago and the return flight from the islands.

The standard program has no fixed departure dates. If your vacation is tied to specific days, plan the sequence of flights, island accommodation availability and visits to optional attractions as one coordinated route, to avoid losing a day through inconvenient connections.

## Preparing for the journey

Light city clothing and shoes suitable for long walks are useful in Rio and Recife. At Iguazu, protect your phone and documents from spray. On Pernambuco's beaches, consult tidal forecasts; for Fernando de Noronha, check the rules for natural areas and the permitted baggage size on domestic airlines in advance.

The combination of beaches and national parks makes this route appealing to lovers of [nature trips in Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) and [Brazilian beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/), although the two themes come to the fore at different stages.

## Frequently asked questions about the private Brazil tour

### Does the itinerary include the Argentine side of Iguazu?

The base program covers the Brazilian side. An Argentine excursion can be booked as an extra; border crossing and document requirements are checked according to participants' nationalities.

### How much time is there for the beaches?

Two nights are planned in Porto de Galinhas and 3 on Fernando de Noronha. On the island, one day is devoted to the 4×4 excursion and another is left free. This combines beach relaxation with a substantial nature program.

### Are domestic flights included in the price?

No. Both domestic and international flights are listed among separately payable services.

### Can I go scuba diving on Fernando de Noronha?

Scuba diving is listed as an optional activity for the free day. Availability, price, weather conditions and participation requirements should be confirmed before booking.

### What is important to check before departure?

Domestic flight connections, documents for an optional visit to Argentina, the environmental fee and protected-area rules on Fernando de Noronha, and weather conditions for activities at sea.

## Coffee tour of Brazil: how the 9 days are organized

The defining feature of this journey is an introduction to **the historic Coffee Valley in Rio de Janeiro state**, combined with classic Brazilian experiences. The tour begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), continues to Iguazu Falls, returns to Rio and only then heads inland toward the old coffee estates. The final stage takes place in the mountain region of [Visconde de Mauá](/brazil/place/visconde-de-maua/).

This tour is for people interested in **how coffee changed the region's history**, what fazendas looked like and how life was organized on old rural estates. It differs from a specialized trip to modern coffee-roasting facilities: the published itinerary does not automatically include barista workshops, professional coffee cupping or a visit to an operating export-processing plant.

## When the coffee-focused days begin

| Stage | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Days 1–3 | Rio: sightseeing and free time |
| Days 4–6 | Iguazu, on the Brazilian and Argentine sides |
| Day 7 | [Coffee Valley](/brazil/place/coffee-valley-rio-de-janeiro/) and fazendas |
| Days 8–9 | Visconde de Mauá and return journey |

The first two sightseeing days in Rio are devoted to Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado and city panoramas. The third day is left free or can be used for additional activities. This is why the coffee program should be assessed by its actual content, not by the nine-day duration of the entire journey.

The route then includes a domestic flight to Iguazu, a visit to the Brazilian side and a separate day on the Argentine side. [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) are in different countries: a border crossing requires checking entry conditions for each traveler's nationality. Brazil remains the tour's principal country, while the Argentine visit is part of its excursion itinerary.

## Three fazendas in the Coffee Valley

The main coffee-focused day begins with a departure from Rio to the [Coffee Valley](/brazil/place/coffee-valley-rio-de-janeiro/). Here the itinerary introduces the history of the state's agricultural wealth and large nineteenth-century estates. The development of coffee plantations was linked to the forced labor of enslaved people; leaving that history out would prevent a full understanding of the region's economy.

Planned stops:

- [Ponte Alta Fazenda](/brazil/place/fazenda-ponte-alta/) — the first stop of the coffee stage.
- [Taquara Fazenda](/brazil/place/fazenda-taquara/) — the next historic estate.
- [Florença Fazenda](/brazil/place/fazenda-florenca/) — a visit in the second half of the day.

Each fazenda has its own history and visiting conditions. Its name in the program confirms a stop, but **does not guarantee that all three estates offer working coffee-processing facilities, separate tastings or meals**. Before booking, confirm the sequence of visits, whether the estates are accessible and how their production history will be presented.

It is helpful to start with the [coffee travel](/interests/coffee-tours/) page and then compare this regional journey with other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/): only some coffee tours combine coffee-related sites with Iguazu and city excursions.

## What the Visconde de Mauá stop adds

After visiting the fazendas, the route continues into the mountainous part of the state. Visconde de Mauá is known for rivers, green slopes and waterfalls. A day here replaces the focus on estate history with nature walks and relaxation. Day nine is reserved for the return transfer to Rio.

When planning the journey, allow for the changing climate: Rio is on the ocean, while Visconde de Mauá is in the mountains. Evening temperatures can feel quite different from those on the beach, so it is worth bringing an extra warm layer and shoes suitable for walking. The exact clothing needed depends on the season and chosen activities.

## Included services and separate expenses

The tour includes accommodation in the hotels specified by the itinerary and private excursions. Domestic Rio–Iguazu–Rio flights, international air tickets, optional excursions and personal expenses are listed as separate costs. When comparing this journey with others, account for **the full budget including domestic flights**, the accommodation category and the program at each stop.

The itinerary brings together several fundamentally different experiences: a city, a natural park on an international border, historic fazendas and a mountain region. Ada Tours coordinates the sequence of transfers and excursions for the particular journey; documents needed for visiting the Argentine side are checked separately according to the client's nationality.

## Who this coffee tour is for

It appeals to travelers interested in coffee history, old estates and rural architecture who also want to see Rio and Iguazu on one trip. For someone seeking an exclusively specialized coffee itinerary with daily tastings and several production facilities, the nine-day program may cover too broad a range of experiences.

If coffee culture is your main motivation, start your comparison with the [coffee tours catalog](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/) and check how many actual days are devoted to plantations, processing beans, estates and tastings. The word “coffee” in the title is no substitute for reading the itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about the private coffee tour

### How many days are specifically devoted to coffee fazendas?

The main visits to the fazendas take place on day seven. The other days include Rio, Iguazu, the Visconde de Mauá mountain region and transfers.

### Does the tour visit Argentina?

Yes. One day is scheduled on the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls. The main route is presented as a Brazil tour; border-crossing conditions are checked according to the traveler's nationality.

### Which estates are included?

Ponte Alta, Taquara and Florença are listed. The exact visiting program and conditions are agreed during trip organization.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. The itinerary lists Rio–Iguazu–Rio flights among separate costs, along with international air tickets and personal expenses.
